title: Where does the compass tip go for a hole in the centre?
description: A square is drawn, its diagonals are drawn to find the centre, and a circle is drawn from that point to make a hole in the middle. Keeko's doubt is that the centre of the square is the middle of the bottom side.
teaching_notes: One idea: the centre of a square is where its two diagonals meet, and a circle drawn from there sits evenly inside the square. Watch for students who take the middle of one side as the centre.

source: Construct a square with a circular hole whose centre is the
video_script.why: A learner finds the centre of a square with its diagonals and uses it as the centre of a circular hole.
video_script.substitution: the book's own square with a circular hole whose centre is the same as the centre of the square
video_script.anchor: a square with a circular hole drawn in its middle
video_script.wrong_answer: the centre of the square is the middle of the bottom side
video_script.wrong_move: puts the compass tip at the middle of the bottom side, so the circle sticks out of the square
video_script.payoff_line: The compass tip goes at the meeting point of the two diagonals.

final_answer.value: The centre of the circle is the meeting point of the two diagonals of the square
final_answer.spoken: the meeting point of the two diagonals

hold_back: Answer: centre at the meeting point
maths_rules: the diagonals of a square join opposite corners
the two diagonals cross at one point, the centre of the square
that point is the same distance from all four sides
the compass tip at the meeting point draws a circle with the same centre as the square
video_script.design: A square is drawn, its diagonals found, and the circle drawn from the meeting point.
